DEVS.doc: Known chimera divergences from RFC 1813, per cell.

known.create-search-perm-1771: POSIX path resolution requires search (execute) permission on the parent before a name can be resolved at all, so CREATE over an existing name in a directory the caller cannot search is NFS3ERR_ACCES ahead of any existence or type result (RFC 1813 3.3.8 read with XBD 4.13). chimera's mkfs backends (memfs/diskfs/cairn) omit the search check on the existing-entry path and leak the type-based reply instead -- EISDIR over a directory, EXIST over another non-regular object, or OK with the existing file's handle for an UNCHECKED create. chimera bug #1771; the passthrough backends resolve through the host kernel and get it right, which is why the model's branch also accepts ACCES.
known.G3-link-dir-badtype: RFC 1813 3.3.15 (LINK; the directory-source status is unspecified).  ganesha refuses a directory hard link with NFS3ERR_BADTYPE where the model -- and chimera -- answer NFS3ERR_ISDIR.  RFC 1813 3.3.15 lists neither ISDIR nor a POSIX EPERM among LINK's errors, so servers differ.  Nothing is linked, so nothing downstream parts.  Replaces the ganesha registry's GN-2-link-dir-badtype.  Note the NFSv4 LINK path is a SEPARATE divergence with a different answer: there ganesha agrees with the model (NFS4ERR_ISDIR) and it is the Linux server that diverges (see S4-link-dir-notdir in quint/nfs4).
known.K3-exclusive-mode-zero: RFC 1813 3.3.8 (the mode of an EXCLUSIVE-created file is undefined until the client's SETATTR).  knfsd creates the exclusive file with no permission bits until the follow-up SETATTR, where the model -- like ganesha and chimera -- uses 0600.  RFC-undefined, so this is a knfsd-specific choice rather than a defect; it is recorded as a deviation because the model has to predict SOME mode for the attribute comparison to mean anything.  Replaces the knfsd registry's KN3-2-exclusive-mode-zero.

T_ERROR_PRECEDENCE.doc: RFC 1813 mandates no error precedence when more than one condition applies to a request. With this on, the two cases the corpus reaches accept the host kernel's order as well as the model's: LINK of a directory onto an existing name (ISDIR or EXIST), and RENAME of a non-directory onto a NON-EMPTY directory (ISDIR or NOTEMPTY). Off means the cell demands the model's order exactly.

T_EXCL_RETRY_VERIFIER.doc: RFC 1813 3.3.8 says an EXCLUSIVE create retry presenting the same verifier 'should' succeed idempotently -- a guarantee for a true RETRANSMIT. chimera stores the verifier in the file's atime/mtime, the mechanism the RFC itself suggests, so on a backend that resolves through the host kernel an intervening READ bumps atime, the verifier no longer matches, and the retry answers EXIST. Permitted, because this is not a retransmit. With this on both answers are accepted; off demands the idempotent OK.
